characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL JEM-2100F HR-TEM with energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) detector
characterization_methods.key_findings: Observed nanoscale Cu-rich phase and κ-carbide; Cu-rich phase is irregular oval (~10 nm diameter) with a small amount of bar shapes (~30 nm length), shows no obvious interface with the austenitic matrix; IFFT shows almost no dislocations and stacking faults in the Cu-rich phase; (002) plane spacing of Cu-rich phase measured as 0.182 nm.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM samples of 3 mm diameter mechanically polished to ~100 μm then twin-jet electro-polished in 10 % perchloric acid alcohol
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine the microstructure and Cu-rich phase/κ-carbide precipitates in the aged 3Cu steel

characterization_methods.key_findings: SAED patterns of Cu-rich phase and κ-carbide in aged 3Cu steel; the text reports the Cu-rich phase has BCC structure (Fig. 1 inset) and that no additional diffraction spots other than those of Cu-rich phase and κ-carbide are observed, indicating coherence with the austenitic matrix; cube-on-cube relationship (111)γ//(111)κ//(111)Cu with zone axis Z=[01̄1].
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Zone axis Z=[01̄1]; 2 1/nm scale bar patterns
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine crystal structure and orientation relationships of Cu-rich phase and κ-carbide

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EDS detector on JEOL JEM-2100F HR-TEM
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe, Mn and Al exhibit brighter contrast within the white dashed box zone (inferred κ-carbide) while Cu is darker (excluded); Cu exhibits brighter contrast within the magenta line area (Cu-rich phase) while Fe, Mn and Al are darker, showing partitioning that drives Cu-rich phase formation near κ-carbide.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Elemental maps of Fe, Mn, Al and Cu over the imaged region
characterization_methods.purpose: Map elemental distribution between matrix, κ-carbide and Cu-rich phase
characterization_methods.technique: TEM energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) elemental mapping

characterization_methods.key_findings: The lattice parameter of the 3Cu steel austenitic matrix under solid solution treatment is a = 0.3689 nm, which is higher than the critical lattice parameter (~0.3670 nm), enabling κ-carbide precipitation.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the lattice parameter of the austenitic matrix

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute the lattice misfit δ between two phases
analytical_models.model_note: δ = |a0 - a1|/a0, where a0 and a1 are the lattice parameters of phase a0 and a1 respectively.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Lattice parameters used for the calculation (a = 0.3652 nm for FCC Cu-rich phase, a = 0.3775 nm for κ-carbide, a = 0.3689 nm for the austenitic matrix) were obtained from HRTEM/SAED and XRD.

analytical_models.equation_role: Empirical index predicting whether intragranular κ-carbide can precipitate based on composition
analytical_models.model_name: Composition boundary formula for intragranular κ-carbide precipitation in Fe-Mn-Al-C steel
analytical_models.model_note: 0.208(wt.%C) + 0.098(wt.%Al) = 1 - 0.0054(wt.%Mn); used to infer that the Mn and C content in 3Cu steel exceeded the critical Mn and C content required for intragranular κ-carbide precipitation.

computational_details.simulation_method: empirical critical lattice parameter / composition boundary criterion
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Comparison with XRD-measured lattice parameters (0Cu a = 0.3687 nm, 3Cu a = 0.3689 nm) against the critical lattice parameter a = 0.3670 nm.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The precipitation of κ-carbide promotes the precipitation of the Cu-rich phase: as κ-carbide precipitates from the austenitic matrix, Cu atoms migrate to the austenitic matrix without κ-carbide, increasing the Cu concentration near κ-carbide; when the Cu concentration reaches a certain degree, Cu atoms gather into Cu-rich clusters which precipitate as Cu-rich phase.

interfaces.interface_notes: All three phases (austenite, κ-carbide and Cu-rich phase) share a cube-on-cube orientation relationship: [110]γ//[110]κ//[110]Cu and (111)γ//(111)κ//(111)Cu. The interfacial energy of κ-carbide with the austenitic matrix is 0.025 J/m² and of Cu-rich phase with the austenitic matrix is 0.086 J/m², both <0.1 J/m²; the lower κ-carbide/matrix interfacial energy means κ-carbide precipitates earlier than the Cu-rich phase during aging.
interfaces.phase_evolution: In the early stage of aging treatment, κ-carbide preferentially precipitates, followed by the Cu-rich phase; the Cu-rich phase precipitates directly in FCC structure.

phase_interfaces.coherence: coherent (lattice misfit 1.0 %, < 5 %); no obvious interface observed

interfaces.slip_behavior: Almost no dislocations and stacking faults are present in the Cu-rich phase (from IFFT analysis).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Solution treatment applied to the Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C-3Cu steel prior to aging; parent process (proc_solution-1000c-1h).
Aging treatment applied after solution treatment; produces the aged 3Cu steel in which κ-carbide and Cu-rich phase co-precipitate.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: TEM foils 3 mm diameter, mechanically polished to ~100 μm then twin-jet electro-polished in 10 % perchloric acid alcohol

structures.microstructure_counts: numerous dark nanoscale precipitates dispersed in the austenitic matrix

phases_present.morphology: irregular oval and a small amount of bar shapes

precipitates.coherency: coherent with the austenitic matrix (no obvious interface)
precipitates.distribution: intragranular, in the austenitic matrix and around/near κ-carbide

size.value: irregular oval diameter ~ 10 nm; bar-shaped length ~ 30 nm

structures.overall_structure: Austenitic low-density steel matrix containing nanoscale co-precipitates of κ-carbide and Cu-rich phase; TEM bright-field shows numerous dark nanoscale precipitates (equiaxed dots to short bars and irregular ovals) dispersed in a lighter austenitic matrix.

unmapped_findings: Lattice parameters of the phases in the aged 3Cu steel: FCC Cu-rich phase a = 0.3652 nm and κ-carbide a = 0.3775 nm; the austenitic matrix under solution treatment has a = 0.3689 nm by XRD.
Cu-rich phase (002) crystal plane spacing is 0.182 nm, consistent with Cu in FCC structure.
The aged 3Cu steel shows a cube-on-cube orientation relationship among the three phases: [110]γ//[110]κ//[110]Cu and (111)γ//(111)κ//(111)Cu.

Interfacial energies in the aged 3Cu steel: κ-carbide with austenitic matrix = 0.025 J/m²; Cu-rich phase with austenitic matrix = 0.086 J/m²; both lower than 0.1 J/m², lower than the incoherent interface value (>0.5 J/m²).

There is a discrepancy in the paper: the Cu-rich phase is described in one place as having BCC structure (Fig. 1 inset) but elsewhere as precipitating directly in the FCC structure and consistent with FCC Cu; the aged 3Cu steel Cu-rich phase is FCC.

The critical lattice parameter of the austenitic matrix is about a = 0.3670 nm; below it intragranular κ-carbide cannot precipitate. Adding Cu to the 0Cu steel increases the austenitic matrix lattice parameter, which is beneficial for κ-carbide precipitation.
